fact: Producing a single pair of jeans requires around 7,500 liters of water — equivalent to 10 years of drinking water for one person.
The fashion industry accounts for 10% of global CO₂ emissions — more than aviation and maritime shipping combined.
Every year, 92 million tonnes of textile waste are generated worldwide. Only 1% of clothing is actually recycled.
Polyester is derived from petroleum and takes over 200 years to decompose. Yet it makes up 52% of all textile fibers worldwide.
Fast fashion produces twice as many clothes as it did 20 years ago. A garment is worn on average only 7 to 10 times before being thrown away.
Organic cotton uses 91% less water than conventional cotton and requires no chemical pesticides.
Textile dyeing is the second largest polluter of clean water globally, releasing toxic chemicals directly into rivers and streams.
Wearing a garment just 9 months longer reduces its carbon, water and waste footprint by 20 to 30%.
75 million people work in the global textile industry. 80% are women, often paid well below a living wage.
Washing synthetic clothes releases up to 700,000 microplastic fibers per cycle, which end up in our oceans.
